title: Finite algebras over a local henselization have finite-type strict local models
statement: Let $D$ be a commutative Noetherian ring, let $R_0$ be a finite-type $D$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], and let $\mathfrak q\subset R_0$ be maximal with separably closed residue field $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ [def-weil-residue-field, def-kun-separably-closed]. Let $H=((R_0)_{\mathfrak q})^h$ be the local henselization [def-weil-pbc-henselization-at-prime], let $\widehat H$ be its maximal-ideal completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and let $C$ be a commutative $H$-algebra finite as an $H$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Suppose $\widehat H\otimes_H C$ is a nonzero local ring [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Then $C$ is a Noetherian strictly henselian local ring [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. There exist a finite-type $R_0$-algebra $F$, a maximal ideal $\mathfrak z\subset F$ over $\mathfrak q$, and a geometric point $\bar z$ of $Z=\operatorname{Spec}F$ supported at $\mathfrak z$ [def-weil-geometric-point, def-weil-affine-spectrum], with an isomorphism of $R_0$-algebras $C\cong\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{Z,\bar z}$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. In particular $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}D$ is finite type and the image of $\mathfrak z$ in $\operatorname{Spec}R_0$ is the specified closed point $\mathfrak q$.

source.place: Expose V, proof 2.2.7 (finite algebra descended from the local henselization); strict-local form in Expose XVII, final paragraph 6.5. The completed tensor being local selects the unique factor.
